title: Chapter 26: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

blocks.content: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is the statutory regulatory body responsible for promoting old-age income security by regulating pension funds in India. It oversees the National Pension System (NPS) and ensures transparency, financial safety, and systematic growth of pension schemes.
The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is the statutory regulatory body responsible for promoting old-age income security by regulating pension funds in India.

items: PFRDA is a statutory regulatory body (often tested in polity/economy questions regarding regulatory institutions).
The National Pension System (NPS) is regulated by PFRDA, not RBI or SEBI.
PFRDA's core mandate focuses on financial safety, transparency, and systematic growth of pension funds.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: PFRDA serves as the statutory regulatory body governing pension funds in India.
Its primary responsibility is promoting old-age income security.
It directly oversees the National Pension System (NPS).
PFRDA is tasked with ensuring transparency, financial safety, and systematic growth in pension schemes.
